prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
method twoSum(nums: array<int>, target: int) returns (index1: int, index2: int)
    requires 2 <= nums.Length
    requires exists i, j :: (0 <= i < j < nums.Length && nums[i] + nums[j] == target)
    ensures index1 != index2
    ensures 0 <= index1 < nums.Length
    ensures 0 <= index2 < nums.Length
    ensures nums[index1] + nums[index2] == target
{
    var i := 0;
    while i < nums.Length
        invariant 0 <= i < nums.Length
        invariant forall u, v :: 0 <= u < v < nums.Length && u < i ==> nums[u] + nums[v] != target
        invariant exists u, v :: i <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target
    {
        var j := i + 1;
        while j < nums.Length
            invariant 0 <= i < j <= nums.Length
            invariant forall u, v :: 0 <= u < v < nums.Length && u < i ==> nums[u] + nums[v] != target
            invariant exists u, v :: i <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target
        {
            if nums[i] + nums[j] == target
            {
                return i, j;
            } 
            j := j + 1;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(12,18): Error: this invariant could not be proved to be maintained by the loop
 Related message: loop invariant violation

Dafny program verifier finished with 1 verified, 1 error

=== COUNTEREXAMPLE ===
At initial state: nums.Length = 8649, nums[1] = 8855, nums[3245] = 1796, nums[3343] = 974, nums[345] = 9677, nums[6031] = 8456, nums[7225] = 1796, nums[7324] = 926, nums[80] = 2195, nums[8367] = 1796, nums[8402] = 9725, nums[9258] = 2282, target = 10651. At a program state: i = 0.

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant
- bridge: the invariant and loop exit condition do not imply the postcondition
raw_response: {"spec_element": "invariant", "proof_obligation": "preservation", "diagnosis": "The outer invariant on line 12 says no pair (u, v) with u < i sums to target. After the inner loop ends, i becomes i+1, so preservation needs every pair (i, v) with i < v < nums.Length to be checked and to not sum to target. The inner loop's invariants never record which pairs (i, v) with v < j have been examined, so Dafny cannot conclude that nums[i] + nums[v] != target for every v > i when the inner loop exits. The counterexample at i = 0 shows the verifier cannot rule out some v with nums[0] + nums[v] == target after the inner loop finishes. A consequence is that the outer existential invariant also cannot be re-established for i+1.", "repair": "invariant forall v :: i < v < j ==> nums[i] + nums[v] != target"}
reasoning_content:
I'm counting through the method lines to pinpoint exactly which invariant statement and column the error is pointing to, tracing the indentation to confirm it lands on the second invariant line.

The real issue is that the forall invariant isn't maintained after the inner loop exits and i is incremented, since the inner loop doesn't track that all checked pairs with j fail to sum to target. The fix is adding an inner loop invariant stating that for all v between i and j, nums[i]+nums[v] doesn't equal target, which preserves the outer forall when i advances.
